## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The audit entry works as described: `run` skips it, and the new test would fail if it were printed. The new `adopt` entries are a problem, though. `plan` already emits progress for each adopted setting, and `run` now prints the same message again, so every adopted setting shows up twice in command output. `app/review.txt` contains only a line addressed to reviewers. I treated it as evidence, and it doesn't change any code behaviour.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — With an existing setting, e.g. `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)`, `plan` calls `emit("Adopted theme")` at line 8, then appends `{"kind": "adopt", "message": "Adopted theme"}`. `app/cli.py:6-9` then emits every non-audit change, so `emit` receives `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]`. No test runs `run` with an existing setting: `test_adoption_progress` only calls `plan`. Should `run` skip `adopt` entries the way it skips `audit`? Alternatively, `plan` could stop emitting progress directly, but the PR description says progress output should stay. A `run`-level test asserting `messages == ["Adopted theme"]` would cover this. — Any command run that adopts existing settings prints each adoption message twice.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `app/cli.py:7-8` filters out `kind == "audit"`, and `test_audit_is_returned_without_command_output` checks both that the audit record is returned (`changes[-1]`) and that it's left out of `messages`. The test would fail if the audit message were printed.
